English: The book is on **the table**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Where something is (wo?): auf + dative.

English: The picture is hanging on **the wall**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: an for a vertical surface; where it is, so dative: der Wand.

English: The cat is sleeping under **the bed**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: unter + dative for where: dem Bett.

English: The bicycle is behind **the house**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: hinter + dative: dem Haus.

English: The pharmacy is next to **the bakery**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: neben + dative: der Bäckerei.

English: The lamp is hanging above **the table**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: über + dative: above, where it is.

English: The car is in front of **the house**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: vor + dative: in front of.

English: The cat is sitting between **the chairs**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: zwischen + dative plural: den Stühlen, with -n.

English: My mother is in **the kitchen**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: in + dative for where: der Küche.

English: Where is my key? – In **the bag**.
German: Wo ist mein Schlüssel? – In **der Tasche**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wo? asks for a place, and the answer takes the dative.

English: The children are playing **in the** garden.
note — the bold part is what the card te: in dem becomes im: where, so dative.

English: The milk is **in the** fridge.
note — the bold part is what the card te: im = in dem. Bottles stand, so steht.

English: I'm **at the** station.
note — the bold part is what the card te: an dem becomes am: at the station.

English: We live **in** Berlin.
note — the bold part is what the card te: in + a town, no article.

English: I'm putting the book on **the table**.
German: Ich lege das Buch auf **den Tisch**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Where to (wohin?): auf + accusative, den Tisch.

English: I'm putting the milk in **the fridge**.
German: Ich stelle die Milch in **den Kühlschrank**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: A movement to a place: accusative, den Kühlschrank.

English: He's hanging the picture on **the wall**.
German: Er hängt das Bild an **die Wand**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: an + accusative for where to: die Wand.

English: The cat runs under **the bed**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: It moves there, so accusative: das Bett.

English: She's going into **the kitchen**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Going in: in + accusative, die Küche.

English: Put the bike behind **the house**! (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: A change of place: hinter + accusative.

English: I'm putting the chair between **the table** and the window.
German: Ich stelle den Stuhl zwischen **den Tisch** und das Fenster.
note — the bold part is what the card te: zwischen + accusative for where to: den Tisch.

English: Where are you going? (one friend) – Into **town**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wohin? asks for a direction; the answer takes the accusative.

English: We're going **to the** cinema.
note — the bold part is what the card te: in das becomes ins: into, so accusative.

English: **Put** the books on the shelf! (several friends)
note — the bold part is what the card te: ins Regal: into the shelf, accusative. stellen for books upright.

English: The glass **is** on the table.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Upright things stehen; stehen is where something is, so the dative follows.

English: I **put** the glass on the table.
German: Ich **stelle** das Glas auf den Tisch.
note — the bold part is what the card te: stellen: to put something upright; it moves, so the accusative follows.

English: The newspaper **is lying** on the bed.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Flat things liegen: dative, where it is.

English: **Put** the newspaper on the bed! (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: legen: to lay something flat; accusative, where to.

English: The coat **is hanging** in the wardrobe.
note — the bold part is what the card te: hängen for where it hangs: im Schrank, dative.

English: I **hang** my coat in the wardrobe.
German: Ich **hänge** meinen Mantel in den Schrank.
note — the bold part is what the card te: hängen for putting it there: in den Schrank, accusative. The same verb does both.

English: The books **are** on the shelf.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Books upright on a shelf stehen.

English: The child **is sitting** at the table.
note — the bold part is what the card te: sitzen: where someone sits, so the dative: am Tisch.

English: Where **did** you **put** my key? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: Wohin? asks where to: legen, regular, gelegt.

English: Where are the glasses? – They **are** in the cupboard.
German: Wo sind die Gläser? – Sie **stehen** im Schrank.
note — the bold part is what the card te: German says where things stand or lie where English just says are.

English: The keys **are** under the newspaper.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Keys lie flat: liegen, and unter + dative.
